chapter: Harlem musicians and the road with Armstrong
title: Russell caught between the band and Glaser, and giving up leadership
summary: Glaser had Russell fire men on the word of job-seekers; Russell tired of the hatred and resigned, and nobody in the band wanted to take over.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: Was Joe Garland in the band?
He'd come in just before we'd taken over...he'd come in the band. He wasn't in the band too long.
Didn't he have a lot to do with the arrangements and looking after the band...the so-called straw-boss?

Well, he was the boss when... See, Russell was tired of the way things was run, and he was in the middle. Russell was in the middle between the band and Joe Glaser. Russell was catching hell from the men in the band plus Joe Glaser.

Joe Glaser would listen to everybody out in the street here in New York, the unemployed musicians tryin' to get jobs, and this-that-and-the-other, and they'd go sing a song to Joe, telling him how bad so-and-so sounded in the band, this-that-and-the-other, "Why don't you let me replace him?" and this-that-and-the-other. Somebody was always shooting for your job. Well, they talked to Joe, and Joe didn't know. First thing Joe wanted to know, "Well, who did you play with?" and they'd name some names and things.

Next thing you know, Russell would get a notice from Joe, or he called him up or something, from Joe Glaser, to let so-and-so go. Now, here's Russell... He's got to fire a man for no reason! As far as Russell's concerned, the man is doing his work and doing his job. But the boss said, "Fire so-and-so-and-so." So what's Russell to do? He's got to let him go. So he gives out the notice. Joe Glaser can't fire him. Joe don't even belong to the union. So Russell got to give him his notice. But he makes himself a bad fellow then.

Well, he gave out quite a few notices, which he had to do. And consequently, the people that he fired, they never liked him. They hated him. So Russell got tired of people hatin' him. And after all, that was Louis Armstrong's name up there in the lights, and he wasn't doin' anything but getting all the glory. And Joe Glaser wasn't firing anybody. That was Luis Russell they'd say fired me. And Russell got tired of that, catching it from both sides -- the band and Joe Glaser.

So Russell, he threw up his hands. He told me... He would play piano in the band, he would just be a member of the band. He didn't want... So that's when Joe got the whole band together, Joe Glaser, and asked us all, one by one, did we want to run the band, because Russell wanted to
give it up -- and who wanted to take it over. Nobody wanted... Nobody wanted to take over the band. He said, "Okay, we'll leave it."
